newsitem.title: USA: White House troubled by congressional aide's exit.
newsitem.headline: White House troubled by congressional aide's exit.

text.p: The White House Wednesday called the resignation of the top lawyer of a House committee probing Democratic fundraising practices "flabbergasting" and said all Americans should be troubled by it.

John Rowley, the lawyer in question, abruptly resigned from the House Government Reform and Oversight Committee Tuesday, saying he had "not been given the authority necessary to accomplish the committee's goals."

"It's a concern when a former U.S. attorney who has been charged with fairly conducting this inquiry says he's not allowed to operate in a professional manner. In a way, that's flabbergasting," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.

Rowley, a former assistant U.S. attorney, had repeatedly clashed with David Bossie, a conservative activist who has spent the last few years trying to discredit President Clinton. Bossie is the committee's chief investigator.

In his letter of resignation, Rowley complained that he had been "unable to implement the standards of professional conduct I have been accustomed to at the U.S. Attorney's Office" in the campaign financing inquiry.

McCurry said if a similiar development had occurred in the Watergate investigation it would have generated an uproar. He cited as an example Fred Thompson, a lawyer for the Senate Watergate panel and now a Republican senator from Tennessee who heads the Senate probe of political fundraising practices.

"If Fred Thompson one day has resigned along with two his investigators and said he wasn't being allowed to conduct himself in a professional manner, there would have been an enormous outcry in this country," McCurry said.
"And I think it has to be troubling to anyone who wants to see a good, measured approach," he added.
